thread:
Maria Chen: Heads up — we started seeing a spike of 413s on /v1/embeddings this morning from a few large customers. Error payloads look like mixed-dimension batches and some single huge vectors.
Tom Alvarez: ugh. Are these the mixed-dims requests where clients send [[768,...],[1536,...]] in the same array?
Maria Chen: exactly. Router rejects with 413 before splitter. Console shows just ‘413 payload too large’ with no hint. Customers are confused.
Ash Patel: can we confirm where the 413 originates? router vs embed-splitter vs model server?
Maria Chen: traces show router responds, code path: pre-parse -> validate dims -> reject. No metric emitted for dims mismatch.
Kevin Wu: that explains telemetry gap. analytics-bot only collects token/latency; no vector-dims histogram.
analytics-bot: noted — missing metric tag: embed.request.dims (currently empty)
Tom Alvarez: two problems: 1) UX for clients (unhelpful 413) 2) router should probably forward to splitter or return structured error with remediation.
Ash Patel: forwarding mixed dims to splitter adds complexity — the splitter currently expects uniform dims per batch. We can change splitter to accept mixed dims and split internally, but that’s a risky change for patch release.
Tom Alvarez: agree risky. Can we instead implement a graceful fallback: router accepts mixed dims and transparently re-chunks into same-dim sub-batches and tag them? Minimal change in router might do it.
Maria Chen: also need payload size protection — some clients send one 1536-d vector but base64 blob causing size > max payload. Router should return structured JSON: {"error":"vector_dims_mismatch","expected_dims":[...],"hint":"set X-Vector-Dims header"} instead of raw 413.
Ash Patel: proposal: 1) immediate (P0): improve error body + docs + console link 2) short term (P1): router-side silent re-chunk into same-dim groups and forward to splitter 3) mid (P2): add dims histogram and per-dims quotas in telemetry/console
Kevin Wu: for 1) I can add a console panel row that surfaces recent 413s by error_code and include example requests (redacted). Also add a KB link in the error response.
Tom Alvarez: what about quota enforcement? When we auto-split we might bypass per-request size safeguards and overload model pools if a single huge upload is split into hundreds of vectors. Need load-shedding rules.
Maria Chen: yes — we should check total tokens or total vector elements post-split and enforce a soft limit with 429 + hint to use async batch job.
Ash Patel: code snippet idea for router re-chunk (pseudo):
```
// router: group inputs by dims
map<int, list<vector>> groups;
for v in inputs:
  groups[v.dims].append(v)
for dims, group in groups:
  chunks = chunk(group, max_batch_size_for(dims))
  enqueue(chunks)
```
We also need to preserve ordering and return aggregated responses.
Maria Chen: ordering + latency fanout is fine as long as we aggregate and stream back. But must instrument request_id to trace sub-requests.
analytics-bot: suggestion: new metrics: embed.requests.dim_count, embed.requests.mixed_dims, embed.rejections.dim_mismatch, embed.rechunked.count, embed.payload.size_bytes.
Kevin Wu: I'll add those to the ingestion pipeline. Also create an alert: if embed.rejections.dim_mismatch > 50/min then page oncall and create a dashboard row with top client IDs.
Tom Alvarez: rollout plan: feature flag the re-chunking behind ff_embed_rechunk and ship improved error body immediately. Canary flag to 1% traffic for 24h, monitor embed.rechunked.count and model latency.
Ash Patel: also need API contract change — recommend adding optional header X-Vector-Dims or X-Vector-Length on client side. If provided, router can validate faster and return actionable message.
Maria Chen: nice. For docs/console UX, error should include: 1) which index in payload failed, 2) expected dims list, 3) sample minimal fix. Eg:
```
HTTP 413
{
  "error": "vector_dims_mismatch",
  "failed_index": 4,
  "got": 1536,
  "expected": [768],
  "hint": "split vectors by dimension or send as separate requests. See https://redwood.ai/docs/embeddings#dims"
}
```
Tom Alvarez: +1 — reduces SRs. Also add a small snippet for SDKs to auto-normalize to mapping: {"vectors_by_dims": {"768": [...], "1536": [...]}}
Kevin Wu: I'll coordinate with docs and support to add KB and to annotate console error links.
Ash Patel: one more edge case: how do we handle mixed-dims in streaming embedding pipelines where clients rely on single response streaming? We should keep streaming behavior by streaming aggregated subresponses in original index order. Might add backpressure for huge numbers of sub-requests.
Maria Chen: agreed. Add a circuit-breaker: if total vectors after split > 10k then reject with 413 and hint to use async batch endpoint.
Tom Alvarez: let's add unit tests for: mixed dims grouping, ordering preservation, aggregated streaming, and quota enforcement.
Kevin Wu: I'll create dashboard panels and an alert rule and drop a link here once done.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/embeds-rechunk -> canary (1%) scheduled at 2026-03-19T09:30:00Z
Maria Chen: thanks — team, please 👍 on the plan if you agree. We'll track infra work in GH issue #3421 and docs in DOCS-789.
Tom Alvarez: 👍
Ash Patel: 👍
Kevin Wu: 👍
Maria Chen: filing follow-ups: docs + console link (DOCS-789), router changes (GH-3421), telemetry + alerts (MON-556).
